title: Layer-Asymmetry-Induced Topological Superconductivity in High-T$_c$ Bilayer Nickelates
authors: Zhongyi Zhang, Congcong Le, Hoi Chun Po, Jiangping Hu, Xianxin Wu, Shengshan Qin
abstract: The recent discovery of high-T$_c$ superconductivity in bilayer nickelates has highlighted the crucial role of interlayer coupling and motivated proposals for dominant interlayer pairing. Whether such pairing can support topological superconductivity, however, remains unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that substrate-supported bilayer nickelate thin films can host an intrinsic time-reversal-invariant topological superconducting phase protected by diagonal mirror symmetry. Using a two-orbital model derived from first-principles calculations, we show that a modest layer-asymmetric potential and layer-staggered Rashba spin-orbit coupling drive the system into this topological phase over a broad parameter range with a dominant interlayer pairing. The nontrivial topology arises from a reversal of the pairing sign on one of the spin-split bonding Fermi surfaces and is characterized by a nonzero mirror winding number along the diagonal direction, as well as a Majorana Kramers pair at the [11] edge. The phase also features bulk gap nodes located slightly away from the diagonal directions, featuring chiral charge and zero-energy flat bands. We discuss experimental routes for realizing and tuning this phase. Our results establish high-T$_c$ bilayer nickelates as a promising platform for topological superconductivity, where tunable topological transitions and Majorana boundary modes can provide probes of unconventional pairing.
summary: This work demonstrates that high-T$_c$ bilayer nickelates can host a topological superconducting phase due to the interplay between layer-asymmetry and spin-orbit coupling. By modeling the system with a two-orbital Hamiltonian, the authors predict the existence of topological invariants and Majorana boundary modes. This establishes nickelates as a promising platform for realizing and tuning topological superconductivity.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the interlayer pairing mechanism in high-T$_c$ bilayer nickelates can support an intrinsic time-reversal-invariant topological superconducting phase.
main_result: The combination of a modest layer-asymmetric potential and layer-staggered Rashba SOC drives the system into a topological superconducting phase characterized by a nonzero mirror winding number and Majorana boundary modes.
method: The analysis uses a two-orbital tight-binding model derived from first-principles calculations, analyzing the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian structure.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as substrate-supported bilayer nickelate thin films, incorporating layer-asymmetric potentials and layer-staggered Rashba spin-orbit coupling into an effective two-orbital Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Topological superconducting phase (Class DIII), nonzero mirror winding number, Majorana Kramers pair at the [11] edge, and bulk gap nodes.
important_parameters: Layer-asymmetric potential strength (V) and Rashba SOC strength (lambda).
main_assumptions: The model neglects the orbital dependence of the substrate-induced terms, and the substrate breaks the mirror symmetry via an interface electric dipole.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup on the substrate, the pairing structure on the Fermi surface, and the band structure showing the effect of SOC.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using first-principles derived parameters, analyzes the resulting Hamiltonian structure, calculates the topological invariants (winding number), and concludes by discussing experimental realization.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between structural asymmetry (substrate interaction) and the emergence of topological superconductivity in a strongly correlated material like nickelates is highly relevant for understanding unconventional pairing mechanisms.
